title: cmate-orchestrate execution plan v2
description: Dry-run execution plan produced by the cmate-orchestrate plan-core runner. Closed schema: an unknown field is a contract violation, not something a reader may ignore. The plan is a pure function of its inputs, so the same input yields a byte-identical plan (Claude/Codex parity). v2 adds issues[].acceptance_gates. Consumers accept a v1 plan too (it simply declares no acceptance gates), but the planner only ever emits v2, so this is the shape that is schema-checked.

waves.description: Ordered waves. Every issue appears in exactly one wave; a later wave runs after all earlier waves complete. That is what the DEFAULT dispatch scheduling does with them. Under `dispatch.mjs --schedule dag` (Issue #183) they become REFERENCE INFORMATION: the dispatcher gates each issue on its own effective dependencies (this plan's `dependencies`, minus the `basis: lexical` edges section 3.1 of plan-contract.md refuses to treat as edges) and admits it as soon as they are completed + verified, so a wave boundary is no longer a synchronisation point. Two things they still ARE in that mode, and neither is optional: `merge_order` is this array flattened, and the packing rule that keeps two file-overlapping issues out of one wave is the rule the dag scheduler re-enforces itself (it never runs two issues that name a file in common at the same time). The planner is unchanged either way — it always computes and emits the waves.

executed.description: Always false: the plan-core runner never executes a command.

gate_id.description: A CommandMate verification gate id. Mirrors GATE_ID_PATTERN in CommandMate's verify config and GATE_ID_RE in dispatch.mjs: an id this rejects is one `send --contract` would reject.

repo_path.description: Repository-relative POSIX path. No leading slash, no backslash, no control character and no '..' segment: a plan must not name anything outside the target repository.

dispatch_defaults.description: Optional repository-level operating defaults for the dispatch runner (Issue #180). Every key is optional and every one is overridden by the corresponding CLI flag; --no-auto-yes is how auto_yes is declined for a single run. no_infer is the planner's flag and is declared here only so one profile holds one declaration.

acceptance_gates.description: Transcription of the issue body's ```acceptance-gates block (references/acceptance-gates-notation.md). Null means the body carries no such block, OR that it carries one the planner refused to read — the two are told apart by the acceptance_gate_block_invalid / acceptance_gate_block_unsupported open question, never by this field. `require` names gate ids that MUST take part in the verdict; it is transcribed in the author's order and is a COPY, not a re-encoding. The planner checks syntax only: it never opens the target repository, so the ids are resolved against `<worktree>/.commandmate/verify.yaml` by the dispatch runner, which refuses the issue before `send` when one does not exist (ADR §3.4).

suspected_files.description: The files the worker is allowed to change: this list becomes the dispatch contract's scope.allow verbatim. Paths under the agent harness (.claude/skills/**, .agents/skills/**, .commandmate/**) are NOT here by default even when the issue names them — a worker able to edit the runner that judges it can pass by rewriting the judge — and enter only when the issue declares them under a deliverable heading (## 対象ファイル), which raises the harness_path_in_scope warning. See references/plan-contract.md section 5.3.

scope_defaults.description: Paths the planner allowed by default because a file the issue DID name mechanically drags them along: the same-directory lockfiles of a dependency manifest (package.json -> package-lock.json), and the conventional test paths of a declared source file (src/session.ts -> src/session.test.ts, src/session.spec.ts, src/__tests__/session.ts, ...; session.go -> session_test.go). Every entry is derived from a declared path — no bare glob is ever added — and all of them are already included in suspected_files. Listed here so a reviewer sees which scope entries the planner added rather than read in the issue. See references/adr-scope-derivation.md.

reference_files.description: Paths the planner read out of the issue and deliberately kept OUT of scope.allow: context the issue only cites (under a 根拠 / 参考 / references heading, or documentation named nowhere else), and agent-harness paths denied by default (.claude/skills/**, .agents/skills/**, .commandmate/**). The worker reads them; it may not write them. A path missing from suspected_files is otherwise indistinguishable from one the planner never noticed, so a drop is reported here rather than discarded. See references/plan-contract.md sections 5 and 5.3.

worktree_id.description: Resolved by `commandmate sync` at dispatch time. Null when sync is unavailable (optional per ADR #1447).

questions.description: Blocking questions for this issue. The dispatch runner refuses an issue carrying any of them unless --allow-questions is passed, so this array — not plan.status — is what stops a run. Each entry also appears in plan.warnings under the private code that produced it: open_question_declared (the issue body's ```open-questions block says the AUTHOR has not decided this; the sentence is transcribed verbatim, in the author's order — references/open-questions-notation.md), open_question_block_invalid (that block could not be read and is NOT treated as absent), acceptance_gate_block_invalid / acceptance_gate_block_unsupported (the ```acceptance-gates block, likewise), no_acceptance_criteria, no_suspected_files, ambiguous_file_candidate, acceptance_requires_tests_but_scope_has_none, unconfirmed_lexical_dependency. Every code but the first is the planner reporting something it could not READ; the first is the author reporting something they have not DECIDED, and it is raised before the others for that reason. See references/plan-contract.md sections 5.4 and 5.5 and references/codes-and-recovery.md.

kind.description: explicit: stated in the issue body. inferred: a consumer of a shared contract, from the heuristic. override: supplied by the caller.

basis.description: What grounds the edge, which is not the same question as who stated it. declared: a human wrote it (every explicit and override edge). file_conflict: inferred, and the two issues name at least one suspected file in common — the reason names it. lexical: inferred from shared topic tokens alone. A lexical-only inference is NOT an edge and therefore never appears in this array: the planner raises the unconfirmed_lexical_dependency question on the consumer instead, so ordering follows only from a statement or from the files. This planner always emits the field; it is not in `required` because it was added without raising plan_schema_version, so a plan.json written by 0.27.0 or earlier — which status.mjs still reads — has no basis on its edges and stays valid. Absent means "written before the distinction existed", never "ungrounded". See references/plan-contract.md section 3.1.
